title: Prospective evaluation of the effectiveness and life quality under UVB-311nm, UVA-1 and Blue-light in patients with atopic eczema
summary:
Atopic eczema (atopic dermatitis, AD) is a chronic, inflammatory, relapsing disease accompanied by leading symptoms such as agonising itching, scratching and the associated difficulty falling asleep or sleeping through the night as well as concentration problems and even suicidal thoughts due to the severely inflamed skin. 
The long-term consequences include a permanent feeling of illness, while obvious skin changes cause shame, lower self-confidence and self-esteem. This has a negative impact on social life and also affects patients' families, who are confronted with the high cost of skin care and the depressed mood of their relatives.
Common forms of outpatient therapy (bath oils, creams, avoidance of various allergens) are often not sufficient for long-term improvement of atopic eczema. In such cases, systemic therapies such as phototherapy (light therapy) are an appropriate option. This form of therapy is often initiated during an acute inpatient stay in a clinic, which experience has shown to be of great benefit to patients. Long-term use of the established ultraviolet (UV)-based therapies UVB-311nm and UVA-1 increases the risk of skin cancer and leads to premature skin ageing. UV radiation can also lead to other side effects such as skin burns, severe irritation, bacterial infections and general deterioration of the skin condition. An alternative to this is therapy using blue light, an ultraviolet-free form of radiation. However, of these three standard therapies established at the Bad Bentheim Specialist Clinic, only little data is available on the effect on quality of life and itching. 
The aim of this prospective study is to observe 150 patients with atopic eczema during an acute inpatient stay to determine the extent to which the patients' quality of life improves under the various phototherapies from admission to discharge. The choice of light source (UVB-311nm, UVA-1 or Blue-Light) depends on the skin findings, the judgement of the treating medical staff and the patient's experience. In addition to phototherapy, all patients undergo intensive local therapy and balneotherapy and, if necessary, systemic therapy is initiated within 12 days.
Furthermore, the aim is to measure not only the impact on quality of life, but also the severity of anxiety, depression and pruritus, as well as the skin findings both on admission and on discharge. Paper questionnaires to be completed are handed out on admission and discharge. In addition, the benefit of the treatment is determined in comparison to the patient's treatment goals.
It is expected that therapy in patients with atopic eczema will lead to an intra-individual improvement in the level of suffering, quality of life and skin condition, as well as an increase in psychological well-being.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis Atopic Exzema 
Acute inpatient stay in the dermatology department of the Bad Bentheim Specialist Clinic
Exclusion criteria:
- Exclusion of persons who are affiliated with the sponsor, study director, or the responsible physician
- Exclusion of patients who, in the opinion of the medical staff providing information, are unable to accurately understand the content and significance of the study and the questionnaires and to complete them truthfully
- Exclusion of patients, who are incapable of giving their informed consent
